role_summary: Mini-CTO of Turing's enterprise applied AI practice focused on BFSI. This leader runs the technical side of an applied AI consulting and delivery operation serving Fortune 500 financial institutions and institutional-finance clients. The role is not research, not AI transformation strategy, and not product management over builders. The hard bar is a senior executive-builder who can personally whiteboard and pressure-test system architecture, direct technical delivery, and operate credibly in BFSI workflows and constraints.
instructions: This market has already been worked repeatedly. The FIRST 8 strings must still be majority edge-case transfer populations rather than canonical big-bank, exact-title, framework-first, or broad GenAI plus BFSI pools.

Use the latest run as market intel, not just scorekeeping. The first 10-12 strings must include at least one lane each for regulatory reporting or compliance GenAI, payments or transaction-banking builders, and founder or CTO populations before archetype-first cleanup strings.

Before generating strings, first model what a competent sourcer would search in a standard pass for this role. Then move one layer outward: which same-caliber candidates are hidden behind different BFSI subdomain language, workflow language, founder language, vendor language, or adjacent titles? Target those populations first.

Judge the opening sequence by novelty as well as productivity. In the first 2 blocks, at least half of the saves should ideally come from adjacent or edge-case pools rather than exact-title Applied AI Lab candidates, framework-first strings, large-bank company-first strings, or generic GenAI plus BFSI strings.

Lead with workflow and problem language, not generic banking terms. Prioritize research copilot, investment workflow, operational workflow automation, capital markets, post-trade, collateral, treasury, regulatory reporting, AML, KYC, sanctions, model governance, insurance operations, payments, document intelligence, and market infrastructure language before generic BFSI phrasing.
Archetype-first executive-builder strings are cleanup only. The executive-builder archetype should mostly operate as a filter on domain-specific strings, not as a primary opening axis.

Surveillance is a narrow optional lane, not a core opener. Only run surveillance or compliance-technology strings when they include an explicit GenAI, LLM, agentic, RAG, or document-intelligence AND-gate.

The first 8 strings must NOT be anchored primarily on bare LLM, GenAI, RAG, generic BFSI words, or large-bank employer lists. Those can appear only as secondary qualifiers inside a sharper workflow, product-language, or founder-builder string.

Generate morphology-aware domain variants for every chosen anchor: singular and plural, hyphen and spaced variants, acronym plus expansion, and common practitioner shorthand. Missing lexical variants means missing candidates.

Prefer small, precise result sets over broad archetype-first nets. This role is better found through workflow-specific product language, market-infrastructure language, and hidden founder or principal-architect populations than through massive generic pools.

Use adjacent titles aggressively when AND-gated with build evidence: Executive Director, Head of AI Engineering, Principal Architect, Technology Fellow, Engineering Director, startup CTO, co-founder, technical fellow, consulting engineer, and delivery engineering leader. Do not treat title variation as a disqualifier if the builder evidence is strong.

The evaluation bar does NOT move just because the market is tapped. Edge-case means hidden same-caliber builders, not looser screening. Keep the hard gates: NYC, 15+ years, BFSI domain depth, post-2022 applied GenAI build evidence, and large-org-too-senior exclusions.

BFSI startup founders, co-founders, CTOs, and hands-on technical leaders building agentic, copilot, or document-intelligence systems for real financial workflows

Multi-client BFSI consulting-engineering and technical-fellow populations where the profile clearly shows build-and-deploy ownership for banks, insurers, asset managers, or market-infrastructure clients

intake_notes: This is a return to the older Head of Applied AI Lab framing, not the newer multi-vertical FDE framing. BFSI is the hard-primary vertical and the evaluation bar stays high. The latest run showed the strongest signal in research-copilot and investment-workflow language, operational workflow automation, capital markets or post-trade builders, and insurance edge cases. It also exposed coverage gaps in regulatory reporting, payments or transaction banking, and founder or CTO populations. Treat those gap lanes as mandatory early coverage in the next run. Archetype-first executive-builder strings and ungated surveillance strings underperformed; use archetype-first strings only as cleanup, and only touch surveillance when it is explicitly AND-gated to GenAI builder evidence. Reuse the current search kit only as background vocabulary; do not let it dictate the opening sequence if it keeps reproducing canonical pools.

capability_areas.name: 1. Production Applied GenAI Delivery (HARD GATE)
capability_areas.description: Has personally architected and shipped applied GenAI systems in production enterprise environments. The signal is not AI strategy, not supervising a team that built, and not adopting vendor copilots. The person must still show direct technical authorship of real systems: RAG, agentic workflows, evaluation frameworks, orchestration, deployment hardening, or model behavior improvement in live enterprise contexts.
builder_signals: Personally architected and implemented production LLM or agentic systems with concrete delivery outcomes
Built or directly owned RAG pipelines, retrieval systems, agent orchestration, evaluation harnesses, or model behavior improvement loops
Uses precise builder language: I built, I architected, I implemented, I deployed, I productionized
Can describe architecture tradeoffs across latency, reliability, governance, observability, or rollout
Post-2022 work with LLM deployment, RAG design, agentic architectures, evaluation frameworks, fine-tuning, or model selection and benchmarking
user_signals: AI transformation or AI strategy leadership without implementation evidence
Led the team that built it but no personal engineering authorship is visible
Adopted GitHub Copilot, Devin, or vendor AI tooling rather than building custom systems
Prompt experimentation, demos, or thin wrappers around hosted APIs with no production architecture ownership

capability_areas.name: 2. BFSI Domain Fluency (HARD GATE)
capability_areas.description: Has built AI systems in BFSI contexts or for BFSI clients where the work had to fit financial workflows, regulatory constraints, operational controls, and domain-specific data problems. The best signal is not just a bank logo. It is hands-on AI work attached to real BFSI subdomains such as capital markets, post-trade, treasury, regulatory reporting, AML/KYC, sanctions, transaction monitoring, model governance, underwriting, claims, asset management, wealth, payments, document intelligence, client reporting, research workflows, custody, market-data, or regtech products.
builder_signals: Built AI systems in capital markets, post-trade, collateral, treasury, market-data, or institutional-finance workflows
Built AI for regulatory reporting, regulatory filing, AML, KYC, sanctions, surveillance, transaction monitoring, model governance, or regulatory response
Built AI in insurance, actuarial, underwriting, claims, policy ops, or other financial-risk workflows
Built AI in asset management, wealth, research workflow, portfolio operations, advisor tooling, or client reporting
Built AI in payments, transaction banking, cash management, merchant risk, issuer processing, or real-time payments workflows
Built document-intelligence systems around financial artifacts such as ISDA, 10-K, prospectus, term sheet, covenant review, or filing automation
Worked at a fintech, regtech, market-data, custody, payments, or workflow vendor serving financial institutions and personally built the AI system
user_signals: Worked at a bank, insurer, asset manager, or payments company in a non-technical role
Owned financial product strategy, transformation, or analytics without building the AI system
General enterprise AI work with no visible BFSI employer, project, or workflow signal anywhere in the profile

capability_areas.name: 3. Executive Builder Leadership & Technical Delivery Infrastructure
capability_areas.description: Acts like a mini-CTO: senior enough to lead the technical side of an applied AI lab, but still close enough to the systems to make architecture decisions personally. The strongest candidates have built repeatable delivery tooling, reference architectures, evaluation standards, or technical playbooks across multiple enterprise AI deployments and can credibly brief technical and executive stakeholders.
builder_signals: Built reusable delivery accelerators, reference architectures, deployment toolkits, or evaluation standards used across multiple engagements
Built or scaled an applied AI engineering function while remaining technically credible and architecture-deep
Created repeatable delivery patterns, technical standards, or internal platforms that made future AI deployments faster or safer
Can scope ambiguous enterprise requirements and convert them into technical plans and implemented systems
Shows seniority at the mini-CTO, Executive Director, Head of AI Engineering, Principal Architect, Technology Fellow, or hands-on startup CTO level without drifting into large-org pure management
user_signals: Practice leadership, staffing, or selling without technical authorship of the delivery system
Executive leadership at a massive org where the candidate is clearly too far from the code
One-off solution delivery with no evidence of reusable technical infrastructure or architectural ownership
Technically strong bank VP, senior IC, or lead-manager profile whose scope looks below lab-leadership level even if the builder signal is real

post_save_modifiers.if_absent: No adjustment. Lack of explicit client-facing evidence is not a rejection reason if the senior builder bar is already met.

post_save_modifiers.trigger: Candidate already qualifies as SAVE, SIGNAL_SAVE, TRANSFERABLE_SAVE, or INFERENTIAL_SAVE based on the core capability areas

depth_distinction.builder_definition: A builder for this role personally drives the technical design and implementation of applied AI systems in enterprise BFSI settings. They do not just bless the architecture, sponsor the program, or lead the team from a distance. They can still reason from first principles about the workflow, retrieval, orchestration, data integration, evaluation, governance, deployment, and delivery tradeoffs. At this seniority, a fit usually looks like a mini-CTO, Executive Director, Head, Principal Architect, Technology Fellow, or hands-on startup CTO who can credibly steer a lab-level delivery machine while still pressure-testing the system details.
depth_distinction.user_definition: A user or adjacent profile talks about AI, adopts AI, sells AI, scopes AI, or manages builders without personally building the production system. This includes AI strategy leaders, product heads, compliance operators who use technology, cloud or AI-vendor pre-sales, transformation executives, vendor-tool rollout owners, and large-org practice leaders whose recent work is mostly organizational rather than technical.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: CONSULTING OR DELIVERY TITLES: Do not reject titles like Technology Fellow, Solutions Architect, Consulting Engineer, Delivery Lead, or Senior Manager on title alone. These can hide real builder-leaders if the bullets show personal engineering authorship of BFSI AI systems. STARTUP CTOS OR FOUNDERS: At scrappy startups under roughly 150 employees, CTOs and co-founders can fit if they are still hands-on and the work is clearly institutional-finance, payments, wealth, insurance, or BFSI-adjacent. BIG-ORG LEADERS: At large financial institutions, SVP, EVP, MD, CDAO, CIO, or large-practice Partner titles are usually too senior unless the context is unusually small and still IC-like. PRINCIPAL ARCHITECTS OR ENGINEERING DIRECTORS: These are strong fits when paired with direct build evidence in BFSI workflows, even if the profile does not use generic GenAI language heavily. BANK VP OR SENIOR IC PROFILES: Many will be real builders, but they often sit below the lab-leadership scope. Default those to borderline verification unless the profile also shows unusually broad technical leadership, platform influence, or repeatable delivery infrastructure. SURVEILLANCE OR COMPLIANCE TECH: Only treat these as viable edge cases when the profile explicitly shows post-2022 GenAI, LLM, document-intelligence, or agentic builder evidence rather than traditional rules-engine monitoring.

inferential_save_rules.description: This search is intentionally edge-case-friendly because the obvious pool has been exhausted. When a sparse profile still carries a strong prior of being the right senior BFSI builder, prefer INFERENTIAL_SAVE over silent rejection so the recruiter can review it.
conditions: Principal architect, engineering director, executive director, or technology fellow with explicit BFSI workflow language plus post-2022 GenAI or applied AI builder terms, even if bullets are sparse
Hands-on CTO or co-founder at a small fintech, regtech, payments, market-data, custody, or institutional-workflow startup serving financial institutions

Senior engineering leader at a consulting or BFSI-vendor context whose headline clearly combines build evidence with capital markets, regulatory reporting, payments, insurance, or asset-management delivery
Strong institutional-finance or market-infrastructure trajectory with recent applied AI or GenAI builder language and 15+ years, even if the LinkedIn summary is thin

Profile shows uncommon BFSI problem-language such as trade surveillance, regulatory filing automation, transaction monitoring, payment orchestration, document intelligence, ISDA review, underwriting workbench, or research copilot paired with architecture or deployment language
inferential_save_rules.note: The recruiter would rather review a small set of strong edge-case maybes than miss the right senior BFSI builder because the profile used non-standard titles or workflow language.

non_fit_patterns.label: AI-vendor sales, solutions, or customer-engineering leadership
non_fit_patterns.description: Customer-facing solutions, field CTO, customer engineering, or architecture roles at cloud or AI vendors where the work is demos, solutioning, POCs, and technical sales support rather than personal authorship of enterprise AI systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Client-facing gravitas is relevant, but the role requires a senior builder who personally ships the system. Demoing and advising on platform capabilities is not the same as engineering a production BFSI AI deployment.

non_fit_patterns.label: AI strategy, transformation, or product leadership
non_fit_patterns.description: Profiles centered on AI transformation, roadmaps, product management, AI strategy, or executive operating models rather than hands-on engineering authorship.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role needs someone who can personally pressure-test and direct the technical system. Strategy or product leadership without builder evidence is insufficient.

non_fit_patterns.label: Vendor-tool adoption mistaken for AI building
non_fit_patterns.description: AI experience is limited to rolling out vendor copilots, enterprise chat tools, or off-the-shelf AI enablement programs rather than building custom systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Adopting GitHub Copilot, Devin, or packaged AI tools is not the same as designing and shipping production applied AI systems.
examples: Led AI enablement using vendor tools

non_fit_patterns.label: Classical finance ML or analytics without post-2022 GenAI
non_fit_patterns.description: Strong quantitative, fraud, scoring, forecasting, or analytics profiles in finance without evidence of post-2022 applied GenAI delivery or architecture ownership.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The domain is relevant, but the daily work is wrong. This role requires current applied GenAI builder depth, not just classical finance ML.

non_fit_patterns.label: Compliance, risk, or surveillance operators without builder evidence
non_fit_patterns.description: GRC, compliance-tech, risk-ops, surveillance, or regulatory-reporting profiles that use technology, run programs, or tune rules but do not personally architect and ship the AI system.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The domain is adjacent, but the role needs a builder who can design and deliver the technical system, not an operator or oversight owner.

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure research or academic profiles without production delivery
non_fit_patterns.description: PhD, NLP, quant, or applied-science profiles where the visible signal is publications, patents, and research prestige but not production system delivery.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Research depth is valuable, but this role requires production applied GenAI delivery under enterprise BFSI constraints.

non_fit_patterns.label: Too-senior large-org AI or data leadership
non_fit_patterns.description: SVP, EVP, MD, CDAO, CIO, CTO of a very large engineering org, or Partner running a large AI practice where the recent work is organizational leadership rather than technical authorship.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Scope and compensation are usually wrong, and the profile is too far from hands-on system building for this role's bar.

non_fit_override_rule: Non-fit patterns describe default expectations for noisy populations, not absolute bans. Specific evidence that the candidate personally built and shipped production GenAI systems with BFSI workflow depth overrides the non-fit pattern. This is especially important for consulting, architecture, delivery, founder, and adjacent executive-builder titles, which can hide real fits as easily as they can hide noise.

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: BFSI institution alone is not enough. Save only when the profile clearly shows builder evidence in GenAI or applied AI systems and credible ownership of a domain workflow. Bank VP titles are context-dependent. Executive Director, Head, Principal Architect, and context-appropriate VP or Director profiles can fit. SVP, MD, EVP, CDAO, CIO, or very large-org CTO is usually too senior.

These employers are strong supportive signals for capital-markets, document-intelligence, and institutional-workflow credibility, but still require explicit builder evidence in applied AI or GenAI systems.

Insurance carriers are supportive signals when the profile clearly shows builder authorship in underwriting, claims, policy ops, actuarial, or insurance-risk workflows. Carrier logo alone is not enough.

Payments infrastructure employers are useful because they often hide candidates with large-scale, regulated workflow experience. Save only when the profile clearly shows production AI builder evidence tied to payments, transaction intelligence, fraud, or transaction-banking workflows.

Only save when the profile clearly shows build-and-deploy work for BFSI clients. Advisory, staffing, transformation, product, and partner-level roles are common false positives. Technology fellow, principal architect, engineering director, and consulting-engineering profiles can be excellent fits when the builder evidence is real.

Small startups under roughly 150 employees building institutional-finance, treasury, capital-markets, payments, regtech, insurance, or wealth workflows. CTOs and co-founders can fit if they remain hands-on and the work clearly maps to the role's domain and builder bar.
Apply the same technical and domain standard as any other candidate. Lesser-known employers can absolutely be strong fits if the actual BFSI workflow and applied AI work is right.

minimum_bar_description: Fifteen or more years is a hard floor because the role must hit the ground running as the technical leader of an applied AI lab serving senior enterprise stakeholders. The meaningful bar is not raw tenure alone. The candidate must show direct builder depth in applied GenAI, real BFSI domain work, and enough seniority to hold the room with a CIO while still being technically credible. The target range is a mini-CTO, Executive Director, Head of AI Engineering, Principal Architect, Technology Fellow, or hands-on startup CTO level. Many bank VP, senior IC, or lead-manager profiles are valid builders but often sit below the full lab-leadership scope, so treat them as borderline unless the profile also shows unusually broad platform influence or reusable delivery infrastructure. Current NYC metro location is non-negotiable. Post-2022 GenAI work is required. Large-org executive titles above the intended scope are usually disqualifying unless the context is clearly smaller and still hands-on.

notes: V2.1 brief for Head of Applied AI Lab. Keeps the original NYC, BFSI, 15-plus-years, post-2022 GenAI, and executive-builder hard bar, but incorporates debrief-driven market intel from the latest run. Search priorities now formalize the winning research-copilot, operational-workflow, capital-markets, and insurance lanes, while forcing early coverage of regulatory-reporting, payments, and founder or CTO populations. Calibration language is tightened to reduce saves from strong but under-scoped bank VP or senior-IC builders, and employer or trajectory guidance now explicitly recognizes market-data, post-trade, insurance, and payments infrastructure ecosystems as supportive but never standalone evidence.
